run.researchNotes: Top-up 1: sectors 13-24 of 41 (CONTINUE for 25-41). Same conventions as the first payload: returns to 31-10-2026 from NSE total-return dashboards; business growth = average of MOFSL Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27 YoY; earningsGrowth3y = MOFSL FY26-FY28 2-year CAGR; demandGrowth3y mostly a 1-year FY27 forecast, with the span in 'years'. Nifty Capital Goods, Nifty India Railways PSU, Nifty Cement and Nifty Power were used where they track the sector better than the bracketed index. Renewable energy's demandGrowth3y is growth in installed RE capacity (FY27 additions over the FY26 base).

sectors.name: Capital goods

returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

business.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27, each YoY; simple average of quarterly growth

tailwinds: Crisil expects capital-goods revenue to grow 12-14% in FY27 on double-digit power-sector capex, especially renewables.
The FY27 Union Budget raised infrastructure spending 11% to a record Rs 12.2 trillion.
risks: MOFSL warns that high commodity prices and the West Asia crisis could squeeze margins even as order books stay strong.
EPC execution is lagging product companies (PL Capital Q2 FY27 preview, Oct-2026).
outlook.source: MOFSL Aug-2026 valuation snapshot (via Business Standard broker-tips PDF) (Capital Goods EPS growth 15.1% FY27E, 26.4% FY28E); Crisil Ratings FY27 capital goods outlook (2026)

valuation.source: NSE Indices published trailing P/E via marketcalls.in NSE index valuation dashboard (20-11-2026). Long-run median P/E 45.87 since 2026; 5-year average not published there.

sectors.why: Order books and power capex keep 20%+ earnings growth visible, and P/E has cooled to 40.9x from a 45.9x median.

sectors.name: Defence and aerospace

returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

business.period: Q2 FY27 single quarter (Jul-Sep 2026) YoY; earlier quarters not reported for this sector
business.basis: MOFSL coverage: Defense (8 companies); MOFSL tracked Defense as a sector only from Q2 FY27

outlook.years: FY26 to FY28 (earnings, 2-year); FY26 to FY29 (defence production target, implied CAGR)
tailwinds: Defence production hit a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore in FY26, up 15.6% (Ministry of Defence).
The government targets Rs 3 lakh crore of production and Rs 50,000 crore of exports by 2029, implying ~19% a year from FY26.
risks: Public-sector units made ~76% of FY26 output, so orders hinge on government procurement timing.
At 54.7x trailing earnings the index sits above its 47.7x median (71st percentile).
outlook.source: MOFSL Aug-2026 valuation snapshot (via Business Standard broker-tips PDF) (Defense EPS growth 16.0% FY27E, 21.2% FY28E); Ministry of Defence release (17-06-2026) and targets restated (04-11-2026); demandGrowth3y derived as (3.0/1.78)^(1/3)-1

valuation.source: NSE Indices published trailing P/E via marketcalls.in NSE index valuation dashboard (20-11-2026). Long-run median P/E 47.73 since 2022; 5-year average not published there.

sectors.why: There is a policy-backed 15-19% growth runway, but the stock prices already reflect it at about 55x earnings.

sectors.name: Railways

returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

bellwethers.name: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation

tailwinds: Union Budget FY27 set railway capex at a record Rs 2.93 trillion, up 10.5% over the FY26 revised estimate.
Railways had used 39% of the FY27 allocation in the first four months (Business Standard, Aug-2026).
risks: Capex growth of ~10% is slower than the earlier boom years, and the index has fallen 29.9% in a year.
The index is PSU-heavy and order inflow depends on a single customer, Indian Railways.
outlook.source: Union Budget 2026-27, Railways Demand for Grants (Feb-2026) via PRS/Tickertape; Business Standard (05-08-2026)

valuation.source: NSE Indices published trailing P/E via marketcalls.in NSE index valuation dashboard (20-11-2026). Long-run median P/E 25.66 since 2024; 5-year average not published there.

sectors.why: Valuations have reset to 19.9x against a 25.7x median, but price momentum is the weakest of any sector.

sectors.name: Infrastructure and construction

returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

bellwethers.name: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone

business.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27, each YoY; simple average of quarterly growth
business.basis: MOFSL coverage: Infrastructure (3-4 companies); Q2 FY27 PAT +233% on a small sample distorts the average

tailwinds: ICRA expects healthy order books to drive a 6-8% construction revenue recovery in FY27.
Construction gross value added is expected to grow 7.0-7.5% in FY27 (ICRA, Sep-2026).
risks: Road-focused EPC firms face volatile order inflows and execution bottlenecks (ICRA).
ICRA expects margins of 10.1-10.6% in FY27 as bitumen and input costs rise on West Asia tensions.

valuation.source: NSE Indices published trailing P/E via marketcalls.in NSE index valuation dashboard (20-11-2026). Long-run median P/E 22.15 since 2007; 5-year average not published there.

sectors.why: Execution is recovering only modestly at 6-8%, and the index trades at its long-run median.

sectors.name: Real estate

returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

business.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27, each YoY; simple average of quarterly growth

outlook.years: FY26 to FY28 (earnings, 2-year); FY27 (residential sales value, 1-year)
tailwinds: ANAROCK projects combined pre-sales of 11 listed developers rising 22.3% to Rs 1.82 lakh crore in FY27.
ICRA expects residential sales value in the top seven cities to grow 8-11% in FY27 on premiumisation.
risks: Area sold is projected to rise only 2-5% in FY27, so growth relies on higher ticket sizes (ICRA).
Ind-Ra sees subdued FY27 growth on a high base and affordability pressure from elevated prices.
outlook.source: MOFSL Aug-2026 valuation snapshot (via Business Standard broker-tips PDF) (Real Estate EPS growth 35.1% FY27E, 30.9% FY28E); ICRA Real Estate update (31-08-2026); ANAROCK (12-08-2026)

valuation.source: NSE Indices published trailing P/E via marketcalls.in NSE index valuation dashboard (20-11-2026). Long-run median P/E 38.59 since 2007; 5-year average not published there.

sectors.why: Listed developers keep gaining share with 20%+ pre-sales growth, but the index has fallen 13.7% in a year at 39x earnings.

sectors.name: Cement and building materials

returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

business.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27, each YoY; simple average of quarterly growth

tailwinds: Cement volumes grew ~10.3% YoY to ~212 million tonnes in 5M FY27 (ICRA).
ICRA expects 6-7% volume growth in FY27 on housing and infrastructure demand.
risks: Crisil sees FY27 margins falling 150-200 bp to 16-18% on 10-12% higher energy costs.
A below-normal monsoon and El Nino could weigh on rural demand (ICRA, Sep-2026).
outlook.source: MOFSL Aug-2026 valuation snapshot (via Business Standard broker-tips PDF) (Cement EPS growth 17.3% FY27E, 14.9% FY28E); ICRA Cement quarterly update (30-09-2026); Crisil Intelligence (13-04-2026)

valuation.source: NSE Indices published trailing P/E via marketcalls.in NSE index valuation dashboard (20-11-2026). Long-run median P/E 28.53 since 2026; 5-year average not published there.

sectors.why: Volumes are strong, but cost inflation and 34x earnings against a 28.5x median have left the index down 21.8% in a year.

sectors.name: Metals and mining

returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

business.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27, each YoY; simple average of quarterly growth

tailwinds: ICRA expects steel demand growth to improve to 9-10% in FY27 on government capex in roads, railways and infrastructure.
Q2 FY27 PAT rose 78% YoY for MOFSL's metals coverage on 28% sales growth.
risks: Equirus notes domestic prices are near the $675/t safeguard-duty threshold, so rising imports may cap price gains.
MOFSL models only 4.9% EPS growth for FY28E after 31.9% in FY27E.
outlook.source: MOFSL Aug-2026 valuation snapshot (via Business Standard broker-tips PDF) (Metals EPS growth 31.9% FY27E, 4.9% FY28E); ICRA Ferrous Metals update (Feb-2026); Equirus (19-10-2026)

valuation.source: NSE Indices published trailing P/E via marketcalls.in NSE index valuation dashboard (20-11-2026). Long-run median P/E 14.22 since 2011; 5-year average not published there.

sectors.why: Profits are surging and valuation sits at the median, but earnings are expected to flatten after FY27.

sectors.name: Oil and gas

returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

business.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27, each YoY; simple average of quarterly growth
business.basis: MOFSL coverage: Oil & Gas (12-14 companies, including OMCs)

outlook.years: FY26 to FY28 (earnings, 2-year); FY27 (petroleum product demand, 1-year)
tailwinds: PPAC projects petroleum product consumption at a record 250.8 million tonnes in FY27, up 2.8%.
Q2 FY27 PAT rose 55% YoY for MOFSL's oil and gas coverage (48% excluding OMCs).
risks: MOFSL models a 12.5% EPS decline in FY27E, so earnings are about flat over two years.
India imports 85% of its crude, so West Asia supply shocks drive margins (PRS).
outlook.source: MOFSL Aug-2026 valuation snapshot (via Business Standard broker-tips PDF) (Oil & Gas EPS growth -12.5% FY27E, 12.5% FY28E); PPAC FY27 demand projection (Feb-2026); PRS Demand for Grants analysis (04-02-2026)

valuation.source: NSE Indices published trailing P/E via marketcalls.in NSE index valuation dashboard (20-11-2026). Long-run median P/E 11.37 since 2020; 5-year average not published there.

sectors.why: It is the cheapest sector at 10x earnings, but forecast earnings are flat and the index is down 13.4% in a year.

sectors.name: Power and utilities

returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

business.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27, each YoY; simple average of quarterly growth

tailwinds: ICRA raised its FY27 power demand growth forecast to ~8.5%; demand grew 11.7% YoY in 7M FY27.
Thermal under-construction capacity exceeds 45 GW as investment in baseload revives (ICRA).
risks: ICRA keeps a Negative outlook on distribution, with limited tariff hikes and loss-making discoms.
Coal stocks fell below normative levels amid rising demand (ICRA, Aug-2026).
outlook.source: MOFSL Aug-2026 valuation snapshot (via Business Standard broker-tips PDF) (Utilities EPS growth 15.0% FY27E, 13.9% FY28E); ICRA Power monthly update (18-11-2026)

valuation.source: NSE Indices published trailing P/E via marketcalls.in NSE index valuation dashboard (20-11-2026). Long-run median P/E 19.47 since 2026; 5-year average not published there.

sectors.why: Electricity demand has rebounded sharply (+11.7% YTD) while the index trades below its median at 18x.

sectors.name: Renewable energy

returns.basis: index (total return); Nifty Energy is dominated by oil, gas and conventional power, so it is a weak proxy for renewables
returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

business.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27, each YoY; simple average of quarterly growth
business.basis: MOFSL coverage: Utilities aggregate (includes renewable IPPs; MOFSL does not split out renewables)

outlook.years: FY26 to FY28 (earnings, 2-year, MOFSL Utilities aggregate); FY27 (installed RE capacity, 1-year)
tailwinds: RE capacity addition was 20.2 GW in 5M FY27, and the sector added a record 50.9 GW in FY26 (ICRA).
Crisil expects 45-50 GWh of battery storage to be commissioned over FY27-FY28.
risks: ICRA expects FY27 additions to moderate to ~45 GW on transmission constraints and unsigned PPAs.
Crisil warns over 35 GW of RE capacity could face grid curtailment in FY27.
outlook.source: MOFSL Aug-2026 valuation snapshot (via Business Standard broker-tips PDF) (Utilities EPS growth 15.0% FY27E, 13.9% FY28E); ICRA renewable energy update (2026, report 7138); Crisil Ratings BESS and curtailment reports (2026); demandGrowth3y = ~45 GW FY27 additions (ICRA) / ~206 GW installed RE at end-FY26 (Crisil)

valuation.source: NSE Indices published trailing P/E via marketcalls.in NSE index valuation dashboard (20-11-2026). Long-run median P/E 14.05 since 2005; 5-year average not published there.

sectors.why: Installed capacity keeps rising, but annual additions are slowing on grid bottlenecks, and the proxy index is falling.

sectors.name: Fast moving consumer goods

returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

business.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27, each YoY; simple average of quarterly growth

tailwinds: Crisil expects organised FMCG revenue to grow 8-10% in FY27, slightly faster than ~8% in FY26.
Anand Rathi expects ~10% revenue and ~14% earnings CAGR for its consumer coverage over FY26-FY28.
risks: Crisil sees volume growth slowing to 2-3% in FY27 from 5-6%, so growth is price-led.
A below-normal monsoon threatens rural demand (Crisil, May-2026).
outlook.source: MOFSL Aug-2026 valuation snapshot (via Business Standard broker-tips PDF) (Consumer EPS growth 7.1% FY27E, 13.0% FY28E); Crisil Ratings FMCG (21-05-2026)

valuation.source: NSE Indices published trailing P/E via marketcalls.in NSE index valuation dashboard (20-11-2026). Long-run median P/E 34.88 since 1999; 5-year average not published there.

sectors.why: It is the weakest large index over a year (-21.7%) on price-led, low-volume growth, though valuation is back at its median.

sectors.name: Consumer durables

returns.source: NSE Indices Index Dashboards (niftyindices.com) for 31-May-2026, 30-Jun-2026, 30-Sep-2026 and 31-Oct-2026; m3 and y1 as printed on 31-Oct-2026; m6 chained as (1+May 1M)(1+Jun 1M)(1+Jul-Sep 3M)(1+Oct 1M)-1. Total-return index, not price return.

business.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27, each YoY; simple average of quarterly growth

outlook.years: FY26 to FY28 (earnings, 2-year); FY27 (room AC volume, 1-year)
tailwinds: ICRA projects room-AC volumes up 12-14% to 12.6-12.9 million units in FY27 after a 10-12% fall in FY26.
Q2 FY27 sales rose 33% and PAT 30% YoY for MOFSL's durables coverage.
risks: Input inflation is forcing 10-20% price hikes, testing demand elasticity (Kotak Securities).
Margins are squeezed because companies cannot fully pass on rising costs (Centrum).
outlook.source: MOFSL Aug-2026 valuation snapshot (via Business Standard broker-tips PDF) (Consumer Durables EPS growth 26.1% FY27E, 23.9% FY28E); ICRA RAC thematic report (30-09-2026)

valuation.source: NSE Indices published trailing P/E via marketcalls.in NSE index valuation dashboard (20-11-2026). Long-run median P/E 67.16 since 2020; 5-year average not published there.

sectors.why: Earnings are recovering at 25%+ and P/E is at its 24th percentile, though still 59x in absolute terms.
